import Shared.QSFactorBaseDimension

/-!
# Round 42, item 3: `Q` is not a free parameter — the factor base *is* the split set

Measurement (round 42, `realqs` execution): every one of the 2,215 smooth sieve
values had all its prime factors in the split set.  This file proves that this is
not an empirical regularity but a theorem, so the quantity `Q(N,B)` that proposal
P4 wanted to move is already *fixed* by the sieve polynomial.

* `legendreSym_eq_one_of_dvd_qsValue` — a prime `r ∤ N` dividing `x² - N` forces
  the Legendre symbol `(N / r) = +1` (for every prime, including `r = 2`).
* `sieveReachable` / `sieveReachable_eq_admissiblePrimes` — the primes `≤ B`
  that divide **some** sieve value are *exactly* the admissible primes of
  `Catalog.Shared.QSFactorBaseDimension`: nothing outside is ever hit, and every
  admissible prime is hit.
* `admissiblePrimes_eq_ramified_union_split` — the admissible set is the
  disjoint union of the ramified primes `r ∣ N` and the split primes
  `(N / r) = +1`.
* `qs_smooth_iff_admissible_support` — a sieve value is `B`-smooth iff its prime
  support lies in the admissible (split ∪ ramified) set; so the column space of the
  relation matrix is pinned to the split set, independently of any design choice
  short of changing `B` or the polynomial.
* `admissible_card_le_factorBase` — `Q(N,B) ≤ π(B)` with the exact deficit being
  the inert primes.
-/

namespace QSSplitForcing

open Finset QSDimension QSRelationPool SmoothSparsity

/-- **Sieve divisibility forces a split prime.**  If a prime `r` with `r ∤ N`
divides a sieve value `x² - N`, then `(N / r) = +1`. -/
theorem legendreSym_eq_one_of_dvd_qsValue {r : ℕ} [Fact r.Prime] {N x : ℤ}
    (hdvd : (r : ℤ) ∣ qsValue N x) (hN : ¬ (r : ℤ) ∣ N) :
    legendreSym r N = 1 := by
  have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
    rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
  exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).2 (isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue hdvd)

open Classical in
/-- The *sieve-reachable* primes: primes `≤ B` dividing at least one value
`x² - N`.  This is the set of columns a single-polynomial sieve can ever touch. -/
noncomputable def sieveReachable (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (factorBase B).filter (fun p => ∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ qsValue N x)

/-- **The factor base is the split set.**  The primes hit by the sieve are
exactly the admissible primes. -/
theorem sieveReachable_eq_admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    sieveReachable N B = admissiblePrimes N B := by
  classical
  ext p
  simp only [sieveReachable, admissiblePrimes, Finset.mem_filter]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hp, x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨hp, isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue hx⟩
  · rintro ⟨hp, hsq⟩
    have hpr : p.Prime := (mem_factorBase.1 hp).1
    haveI : NeZero p := ⟨hpr.ne_zero⟩
    exact ⟨hp, (exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare N).2 hsq⟩

open Classical in
/-- **Ramified ∪ split decomposition.**  The admissible primes are exactly the
primes `r ≤ B` with `r ∣ N` together with those with `(N / r) = +1`. -/
theorem admissiblePrimes_eq_ramified_union_split (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    admissiblePrimes N B =
      (factorBase B).filter (fun r : ℕ => (r : ℤ) ∣ N) ∪
      (factorBase B).filter (fun r : ℕ => ∃ h : r.Prime,
        @legendreSym r ⟨h⟩ N = 1) := by
  ext r
  simp only [admissiblePrimes, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_filter]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hr, hsq⟩
    have hpr : r.Prime := (mem_factorBase.1 hr).1
    haveI : Fact r.Prime := ⟨hpr⟩
    by_cases hN : (r : ℤ) ∣ N
    · exact Or.inl ⟨hr, hN⟩
    · refine Or.inr ⟨hr, hpr, ?_⟩
      have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
        rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
      exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).2 hsq
  · rintro (⟨hr, hN⟩ | ⟨hr, hpr, hleg⟩)
    · refine ⟨hr, ⟨0, ?_⟩⟩
      rw [(ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd N r).2 hN]; ring
    · haveI : Fact r.Prime := ⟨hpr⟩
      refine ⟨hr, ?_⟩
      have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0
        have : legendreSym r N = 0 := (legendreSym.eq_zero_iff r N).2 h0
        rw [this] at hleg; exact absurd hleg (by norm_num)
      exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).1 hleg

/-- **Smoothness of a sieve value is smoothness over the split set.**  For a
sieve value `v = x² - N`, being `B`-smooth is equivalent to having its
whole prime support inside the admissible set. -/
theorem qs_smooth_iff_admissible_support {B : ℕ} {N x : ℤ} {v : ℕ}
    (hval : (v : ℤ) = x ^ 2 - N) :
    (∀ p ∈ v.primeFactors, p ≤ B) ↔ v.primeFactors ⊆ admissiblePrimes N B := by
  constructor
  · intro hsm p hp
    have hfac : v.factorization p ≠ 0 := by
      rw [← Finsupp.mem_support_iff, Nat.support_factorization]; exact hp
    exact smooth_qsValue_support hval hsm p hfac
  · intro hsub p hp
    exact (mem_factorBase.1 (admissiblePrimes_subset N B (hsub hp))).2

open Classical in
/-- `Q(N,B) ≤ π(B)`, with the deficit counted exactly by the primes that are
neither ramified nor split (the inert primes). -/
theorem admissible_card_add_inert (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    (admissiblePrimes N B).card +
      ((factorBase B).filter (fun p => ¬ IsSquare ((N : ZMod p)))).card =
      (factorBase B).card := by
  classical
  unfold admissiblePrimes
  exact Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _

theorem admissible_card_le_factorBase (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    (admissiblePrimes N B).card ≤ (factorBase B).card :=
  Finset.card_le_card (admissiblePrimes_subset N B)

import Mathlib
import Computation.QSSplitSetForcing

/-!
# Round 42, items 1–2: the smooth yield is governed by `Q`, not by `π(B)` alone

Round 42 measured that, at matched `u = log X / log B`, the sieve's smooth density
is essentially uncorrelated with `ρ(u)` (`+0.029`) and strongly correlated with
`Q/π(B)` (`+0.882`), and that paid sieve work *decreases* as `Q` grows.  This file
proves the unconditional skeleton of both observations.

**Smooth counting over an arbitrary prime set.**  `psiS S X` counts `n ∈ [1, X]`
whose prime support lies in `S` (so `psiS (factorBase B) X = Ψ(X, B)`).

* `psiS_mono` — `psiS` is monotone in the prime set.
* `psiS_insert_ge` — **the multiplicative step**: adjoining a new prime `p`
  gives `Ψ_{S∪{p}}(X) ≥ Ψ_S(X) + Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋)`.
* `two_pow_card_le_psiS` — **exponential floor**: if `∏ S ≤ X` then
  `2^{|S|} ≤ Ψ_S(X)` (all square-free sub-products).
* `psiS_le_pow_card` — **exponential ceiling**: `Ψ_S(X) ≤ (log₂ X + 1)^{|S|}`.

So at a fixed value size `X` (fixed `u`), the count is squeezed between two
functions that are exponential in `|S|` — the *exponent* is the size of the
prime set, and nothing else about `B` enters.

**Specialisation to the sieve.**

* `qsYield_le_psiS_admissible` / `qsYield_le_pow_Q` — the number of `B`-smooth
  sieve values `x² - N` on a window `[a, b]` (with `a² > N`) is at most
  `Ψ_{A}(b² - N) ≤ (log₂(b² - N) + 1)^{Q(N,B)}`: the ceiling is governed by
  `Q(N,B)`, the split-set size, *not* by `π(B)`.  Two moduli with the same `B` and
  the same window (hence the same `u`) can therefore have yield ceilings differing
  by the factor `(log₂ X + 1)^{π(B)(Q₁/π(B) - Q₂/π(B))}` — this is the formal
  shadow of "Dickman is blind to `Q`".

**The sign-flip criterion.**

* `work_mono_iff` — in the cost model `work(S) = (|S| + 1) / Ψ_S(X)` (positions
  per guaranteed dependence at fixed `X`), adjoining a prime lowers the work iff
  `(|S| + 1)(Ψ_{S∪{p}} - Ψ_S) ≥ Ψ_S`.
* `work_decreases_of_marginal` — the multiplicative step makes this hold as soon
  as `(|S| + 1) · Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋) ≥ Ψ_S(X)`: one more column is paid for by the
  additive `+1` in the relation target, while it buys a *multiplicative* gain in
  the smooth count.  This is the structural reason why "shrinking `Q` to shrink
  the linear algebra moves the wrong term".
-/

namespace QSSplitYield

open Finset

/-- `Ψ_S(X)`: the number of `n ∈ [1, X]` all of whose prime factors lie in `S`. -/
def psiS (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S)).card

theorem psiS_mono {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : S ⊆ T) (X : ℕ) : psiS S X ≤ psiS T X := by
  unfold psiS
  apply Finset.card_le_card
  intro n hn
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hn ⊢
  exact ⟨hn.1, hn.2.trans h⟩

/-- `psiS` over the factor base is the classical `Ψ(X, B)` of the catalog. -/
theorem psiS_factorBase (B X : ℕ) :
    psiS (SmoothSparsity.factorBase B) X = (SmoothSparsity.smoothPool B X).card := by
  unfold psiS SmoothSparsity.smoothPool
  congr 1
  apply Finset.filter_congr
  intro n _
  constructor
  · intro h p hp; exact (SmoothSparsity.mem_factorBase.1 (h hp)).2
  · intro h p hp
    exact SmoothSparsity.mem_factorBase.2 ⟨Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp, h p hp⟩

/-- **The multiplicative step.**  Adjoining a new prime `p ∉ S` adds at least
`Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋)` new smooth numbers (namely `p · m`). -/
theorem psiS_insert_ge {S : Finset ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpS : p ∉ S) (X : ℕ) :
    psiS S X + psiS S (X / p) ≤ psiS (insert p S) X := by
  classical
  set A := (Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S) with hA
  set C := (Finset.Icc 1 (X / p)).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S) with hC
  set D := (Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ insert p S) with hD
  have hp0 : 0 < p := hp.pos
  have hCimg : C.image (fun m => p * m) ⊆ D := by
    intro n hn
    obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hn
    simp only [hC, hD, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hm ⊢
    have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by omega
    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (Nat.mul_ne_zero hp.ne_zero hm0)
    · have := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hp0).1 hm.1.2
      linarith [mul_comm m p]
    · rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul hp.ne_zero hm0, hp.primeFactors]
      exact Finset.union_subset (by simp) (hm.2.trans (Finset.subset_insert _ _))
  have hAD : A ⊆ D := by
    intro n hn
    simp only [hA, hD, Finset.mem_filter] at hn ⊢
    exact ⟨hn.1, hn.2.trans (Finset.subset_insert _ _)⟩
  have hdisj : Disjoint A (C.image (fun m => p * m)) := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro n hnA hnC
    obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hnC
    simp only [hA, hC, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hnA hm
    have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by omega
    apply hpS
    apply hnA.2
    rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul hp.ne_zero hm0, hp.primeFactors]
    simp
  have hcardC : (C.image (fun m => p * m)).card = C.card :=
    Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun a b h => Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hp0 h)
  have := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.union_subset hAD hCimg)
  rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, hcardC] at this
  exact this

/-- **Exponential floor.**  If every element of `S` is prime and `∏ S ≤ X`, then
`2^{|S|} ≤ Ψ_S(X)`: the `2^{|S|}` square-free sub-products are distinct and
`S`-smooth. -/
theorem two_pow_card_le_psiS {S : Finset ℕ} (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime) {X : ℕ}
    (hX : ∏ p ∈ S, p ≤ X) : 2 ^ S.card ≤ psiS S X := by
  classical
  rw [← Finset.card_powerset]
  unfold psiS
  refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun T => ∏ p ∈ T, p) ?_ ?_
  · intro T hT
    have hTS : T ⊆ S := Finset.mem_powerset.1 hT
    have hTp : ∀ p ∈ T, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (hTS hp)
    dsimp only
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc]
    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2
        (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.2 (fun p hp => (hTp p hp).ne_zero))
    · refine le_trans ?_ hX
      exact Finset.prod_le_prod_of_subset_of_one_le' hTS
        (fun i hi _ => (hS i hi).one_lt.le)
    · rw [Nat.primeFactors_prod hTp]; exact hTS
  · intro T hT U hU hTU
    have hTp : ∀ p ∈ T, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (Finset.mem_powerset.1 hT hp)
    have hUp : ∀ p ∈ U, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (Finset.mem_powerset.1 hU hp)
    have := congrArg Nat.primeFactors hTU
    simp only at this
    rwa [Nat.primeFactors_prod hTp, Nat.primeFactors_prod hUp] at this

/-- **Exponential ceiling.**  `Ψ_S(X) ≤ (log₂ X + 1)^{|S|}`. -/
theorem psiS_le_pow_card (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) :
    psiS S X ≤ (Nat.log 2 X + 1) ^ S.card := by
  classical
  set k := Nat.log 2 X with hk
  set f : ℕ → (S → Fin (k + 1)) :=
    fun n p => ⟨min (n.factorization p) k, by omega⟩ with hf
  have hinj : Set.InjOn f ((Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S)) := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha hb
    have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hb0 : b ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hfa : ∀ p, a.factorization p = b.factorization p := by
      intro p
      by_cases hp : p ∈ S
      · have := congrFun hab ⟨p, hp⟩
        simp only [hf, Fin.mk.injEq] at this
        have h1 := SmoothSparsity.factorization_le_log_two (p := p) ha0 ha.1.2
        have h2 := SmoothSparsity.factorization_le_log_two (p := p) hb0 hb.1.2
        omega
      · have hA : a.factorization p = 0 := by
          by_contra hcon
          exact hp (ha.2 (by rw [← Nat.support_factorization]; exact Finsupp.mem_support_iff.2 hcon))
        have hB : b.factorization p = 0 := by
          by_contra hcon
          exact hp (hb.2 (by rw [← Nat.support_factorization]; exact Finsupp.mem_support_iff.2 hcon))
        rw [hA, hB]
    exact Nat.factorization_inj ha0 hb0 (Finsupp.ext hfa)
  unfold psiS
  calc _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (S → Fin (k + 1))).card :=
        Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn f (fun n _ => Finset.mem_univ _) hinj
    _ = (k + 1) ^ S.card := by simp

/-! ## The sieve yield is bounded by a function of `Q(N,B)` -/

/-- The number of sieve positions `x ∈ [a, b]` whose value `x² - N` is
`B`-smooth. -/
def qsYield (N B a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc a b).filter (fun x => ∀ p ∈ (x ^ 2 - N).primeFactors, p ≤ B)).card

/-- **Yield ceiling by the split set.**  On a window `[a, b]` with `N < a²`, the
`B`-smooth yield is at most `Ψ_{A(N,B)}(b² - N)`. -/
theorem qsYield_le_psiS_admissible (N B a b : ℕ) (ha : N < a ^ 2) :
    qsYield N B a b ≤ psiS (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) B) (b ^ 2 - N) := by
  classical
  unfold qsYield psiS
  refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun x => x ^ 2 - N) ?_ ?_
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx
    obtain ⟨⟨hax, hxb⟩, hsm⟩ := hx
    have hxa : a ^ 2 ≤ x ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hax 2
    have hxb2 : x ^ 2 ≤ b ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hxb 2
    dsimp only
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc]
    refine ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
    have hval : ((x ^ 2 - N : ℕ) : ℤ) = (x : ℤ) ^ 2 - (N : ℤ) := by
      push_cast [show N ≤ x ^ 2 by omega]; ring
    exact (QSSplitForcing.qs_smooth_iff_admissible_support hval).1 hsm
  · intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx hy hxy
    have hx2 : a ^ 2 ≤ x ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hx.1.1 2
    have hy2 : a ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hy.1.1 2
    have : x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 := by omega
    exact Nat.pow_left_injective (by norm_num) this

/-- **The yield ceiling depends on `Q`, not on `π(B)`.** -/
theorem qsYield_le_pow_Q (N B a b : ℕ) (ha : N < a ^ 2) :
    qsYield N B a b ≤
      (Nat.log 2 (b ^ 2 - N) + 1) ^ (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) B).card :=
  (qsYield_le_psiS_admissible N B a b ha).trans (psiS_le_pow_card _ _)

/-! ## The sign-flip criterion -/

/-- Model cost: positions per guaranteed dependence, `(|S| + 1) / Ψ_S(X)`. -/
noncomputable def work (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) : ℚ := ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) / (psiS S X : ℚ)

/-- **Criterion.**  For `p ∉ S` with `Ψ_S(X) > 0`, adjoining `p` does not raise
the model work iff `(|S| + 1)(Ψ_{S∪{p}} - Ψ_S) ≥ Ψ_S`. -/
theorem work_mono_iff {S : Finset ℕ} {p X : ℕ} (hpS : p ∉ S)
    (hpos : 0 < psiS S X) (hpos' : 0 < psiS (insert p S) X) :
    work (insert p S) X ≤ work S X ↔
      (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * ((psiS (insert p S) X : ℚ) - psiS S X) := by
  unfold work
  rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hpS, div_le_div_iff₀ (by exact_mod_cast hpos')
    (by exact_mod_cast hpos)]
  push_cast
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/-- **The sign flip.**  If the marginal prime satisfies
`(|S| + 1) · Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋) ≥ Ψ_S(X)`, then adjoining it (raising `Q` by one) does not
increase the model work. -/
theorem work_decreases_of_marginal {S : Finset ℕ} {p X : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpS : p ∉ S)
    (hpos : 0 < psiS S X) (hmarg : psiS S X ≤ (S.card + 1) * psiS S (X / p)) :
    work (insert p S) X ≤ work S X := by
  have hstep := psiS_insert_ge hp hpS X
  have hpos' : 0 < psiS (insert p S) X := by omega
  rw [work_mono_iff hpS hpos hpos']
  have h1 : (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) := by
    exact_mod_cast hmarg
  have h2 : (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) ≤ (psiS (insert p S) X : ℚ) - psiS S X := by
    have : ((psiS S X + psiS S (X / p) : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ psiS (insert p S) X := by
      exact_mod_cast hstep
    push_cast at this; linarith
  calc (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) := h1
    _ ≤ _ := by
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2; positivity

`S = {2, 3}`, `X = 100`, `p = 5`.  `Ψ_{2,3}(100) = 20`, `Ψ_{2,3}(20) = 10`, so
the marginal condition `3 · 10 ≥ 20` holds and
`work({2,3,5}) = 4/34 < 3/20 = work({2,3})` (indeed `Ψ_{2,3,5}(100) = 34`). -/

theorem lab_psi23_100 : psiS {2, 3} 100 = 20 := by native_decide
theorem lab_psi23_20 : psiS {2, 3} (100 / 5) = 10 := by native_decide
theorem lab_psi235_100 : psiS {5, 2, 3} 100 = 34 := by native_decide

/-- The marginal criterion certifies the flip without computing `Ψ_{2,3,5}`. -/
example : work (insert 5 {2, 3}) 100 ≤ work {2, 3} 100 :=
  work_decreases_of_marginal (by norm_num) (by decide) (by rw [lab_psi23_100]; norm_num)
    (by rw [lab_psi23_100, lab_psi23_20]; decide)

/-- And the strict inequality from the measured counts. -/
example : work (insert 5 {2, 3}) 100 < work {2, 3} 100 := by
  unfold work
  rw [show (insert 5 {2, 3} : Finset ℕ) = {5, 2, 3} from rfl, lab_psi235_100, lab_psi23_100]
  norm_num

end QSSplitYield

import Mathlib
import Shared.QSFactorBaseDimension

/-!
# Round 42, item 4: which way does `rank ≤ Q` point?  The prefix-rank identity

The sieve produces relation (exponent) vectors `v₀, v₁, v₂, …` in `𝔽₂^Q`, where
`Q = Q(N,B)` is the number of admissible primes (`Catalog.Computation.QSSplitSetForcing`).
`k_success` is the length of the *shortest* prefix that is linearly dependent.
Round 42 asserted that the chain `k_success ≤ rank + 1 ≤ Q + 1` "has its first
inequality backwards".  This file settles the question exactly, over any field,
and finds that **both readings are right about different ranks**:

* `prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent` — for any dependent prefix of length `k`,
  `rank(prefix k) + 1 ≤ k` (round 42's correction, for the *prefix* rank);
* `kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one` — the **identity**
  `k_success = rank(prefix k_success) + 1`: at the first dependence the two sides
  meet;
* `kSuccess_le_rank_add_one` — for every collected matrix `M = prefix n` with
  `n ≥ k_success`, `k_success ≤ rank(M) + 1` (so the original chain is *true* when
  `rank` means the rank of all relations collected);
* `kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one` — `k_success ≤ Q + 1`;
* `kSuccess_basis` — the bound `Q + 1` is attained (standard basis first), so the
  empirical ratios `k_success/Q ≈ 0.78/0.71/0.60` are properties of the instances,
  not of the algebra.

The bound counts **relations**, not sieve positions: nothing here bounds the
paid work, which is the number of positions needed to *find* `k_success`
relations.
-/

namespace QSPrefixRank

open Module

variable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]

/-- The first `k` relation vectors, as a family indexed by `Fin k`. -/
def pre (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : Fin k → V := fun i => v i

/-- Rank of the first `k` relation vectors. -/
noncomputable def prefixRank (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Set.finrank K (Set.range (pre v k))

omit [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] in
theorem range_pre_mono (v : ℕ → V) {k m : ℕ} (h : k ≤ m) :
    Set.range (pre v k) ⊆ Set.range (pre v m) := by
  rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨⟨i, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 h⟩, rfl⟩

theorem prefixRank_le (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ k := by
  have := finrank_range_le_card (R := K) (pre v k)
  simpa [prefixRank] using this

theorem prefixRank_mono (v : ℕ → V) {k m : ℕ} (h : k ≤ m) :
    prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ prefixRank (K := K) v m := by
  unfold prefixRank Set.finrank
  haveI : FiniteDimensional K (Submodule.span K (Set.range (pre v m))) :=
    FiniteDimensional.span_of_finite K (Set.finite_range _)
  exact Submodule.finrank_mono (Submodule.span_mono (range_pre_mono v h))

/-- Independence of a prefix is exactly "rank = length". -/
theorem linearIndependent_pre_iff (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) :
    LinearIndependent K (pre v k) ↔ prefixRank (K := K) v k = k := by
  rw [linearIndependent_iff_card_eq_finrank_span, Fintype.card_fin, prefixRank]
  exact eq_comm

/-- **Round 42's direction correction.**  A dependence at prefix `k` forces
`rank(prefix k) + 1 ≤ k`. -/
theorem prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (h : ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k)) : prefixRank (K := K) v k + 1 ≤ k := by
  rw [linearIndependent_pre_iff] at h
  have := prefixRank_le (K := K) v k
  omega

/-- More than `dim V` relations are always dependent. -/
theorem dependent_of_finrank_lt [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : finrank K V < k) : ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k) := by
  intro hli
  have := hli.fintype_card_le_finrank
  rw [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

theorem exists_dependent [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    ∃ k, ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k) :=
  ⟨finrank K V + 1, dependent_of_finrank_lt v (Nat.lt_succ_self _)⟩

open Classical in
/-- `k_success`: the length of the shortest dependent prefix. -/
noncomputable def kSuccess [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) : ℕ :=
  Nat.find (exists_dependent (K := K) v)

theorem kSuccess_dependent [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v)) := by
  classical
  exact Nat.find_spec (exists_dependent (K := K) v)

theorem independent_of_lt_kSuccess [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < kSuccess (K := K) v) : LinearIndependent K (pre v k) := by
  classical
  by_contra h
  exact Nat.find_min (exists_dependent (K := K) v) hk h

theorem kSuccess_pos [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) : 0 < kSuccess (K := K) v := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (kSuccess (K := K) v) with h | h
  · have hd := kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v
    rw [h] at hd
    exact absurd (linearIndependent_empty_type) hd
  · exact h

/-- **The prefix-rank identity.**  `k_success = rank(prefix k_success) + 1`. -/
theorem kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v = prefixRank (K := K) v (kSuccess (K := K) v) + 1 := by
  set k := kSuccess (K := K) v with hk
  have hpos : 0 < k := kSuccess_pos (K := K) v
  have hup : prefixRank (K := K) v k + 1 ≤ k :=
    prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent v (kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v)
  have hind : LinearIndependent K (pre v (k - 1)) :=
    independent_of_lt_kSuccess v (by omega)
  have hr : prefixRank (K := K) v (k - 1) = k - 1 := (linearIndependent_pre_iff v _).1 hind
  have hmono := prefixRank_mono (K := K) v (Nat.sub_le k 1)
  omega

/-- **The original chain, for the full collected matrix.**  If `n ≥ k_success`
relations have been collected, `k_success ≤ rank(M) + 1` where `M = prefix n`. -/
theorem kSuccess_le_rank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ n) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ prefixRank (K := K) v n + 1 := by
  have h1 := kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one (K := K) v
  have h2 := prefixRank_mono (K := K) v hn
  omega

theorem prefixRank_le_finrank [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) :
    prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ finrank K V := by
  unfold prefixRank Set.finrank
  exact Submodule.finrank_le _

/-- `k_success ≤ Q + 1` with `Q = dim V`. -/
theorem kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ finrank K V + 1 := by
  have h1 := kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one (K := K) v
  have h2 := prefixRank_le_finrank (K := K) v (kSuccess (K := K) v)
  omega

/-- **Sharpness.**  In `K^Q`, if the first `Q` relations are the standard basis,
then `k_success = Q + 1`. -/
theorem kSuccess_basis (Q : ℕ) (v : ℕ → (Fin Q → K))
    (hv : ∀ i : Fin Q, v i = Pi.single i 1) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v = Q + 1 := by
  have hle := kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one (K := K) v
  rw [finrank_fin_fun] at hle
  have hind : LinearIndependent K (pre v Q) := by
    have : pre v Q = fun i : Fin Q => (Pi.basisFun K (Fin Q)) i := by
      funext i; simp [pre, hv i]
    rw [this]; exact (Pi.basisFun K (Fin Q)).linearIndependent
  by_contra hne
  have hlt : Q < kSuccess (K := K) v := by
    by_contra hge
    push_neg at hge
    have hdep := kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v
    have hsub : LinearIndependent K (pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v)) := by
      have hcomp : pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v) =
          pre v Q ∘ Fin.castLE hge := by funext i; rfl
      rw [hcomp]; exact hind.comp _ (Fin.castLE_injective hge)
    exact hdep hsub
  omega

/-! ## Specialisation to the quadratic sieve: `Q(N,B) + 1` relations -/

/-- **QS form.**  For relation vectors in `𝔽₂^{A}`, `A` the admissible primes of
`N` at bound `B`, the first dependence occurs after at most `Q(N,B) + 1`
relations, and exactly one more than the rank of the prefix it closes. -/
theorem qs_kSuccess_bounds (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ)
    (v : ℕ → (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes N B → ZMod 2)) :
    kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v = prefixRank (K := ZMod 2) v (kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v) + 1 ∧
    kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v ≤ (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes N B).card + 1 := by
  refine ⟨kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one v, ?_⟩
  have := kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one (K := ZMod 2) v
  rwa [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, Fintype.card_coe] at this

end QSPrefixRank

import Mathlib

/-!
# Round 42, item 6: the `𝔽₂`-rank trap, and which test matrices can catch it

Round 42 found that two library routines silently returned the rank over `ℚ`
when asked for the rank over `GF(2)` (returning `3` on a matrix of `𝔽₂`-rank `2`),
and that "validation passed" was unfalsifiable until a mutation test was added.
This file makes both observations exact.

* `rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero` — over any field, a square matrix has full rank
  iff its determinant is nonzero.
* `rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det` / `rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero` — for an
  integer matrix `A`, full `𝔽₂`-rank ⇔ `det A` odd; full `ℚ`-rank ⇔ `det A ≠ 0`.
* `full_rank_agree_iff` — **the discriminating-test criterion**: a square integer
  test matrix can distinguish a "rank over `ℚ`" instrument from a correct
  "rank over `𝔽₂`" one *on the full-rank question* iff `det A` is a **nonzero even**
  integer.  A validation suite built from matrices with odd (or zero) determinant
  is blind to the bug, which is why the bug survived inspection.
* `trap3_rank_rat` / `trap3_rank_zmod2` — the round-42 witness: the `3 × 3`
  cycle-incidence matrix has `ℚ`-rank `3` and `𝔽₂`-rank `2`.
* `rank_submatrix_le_of_field` — rank does not increase under taking an arbitrary
  submatrix (rows and columns), the tool used for the lower bound.
* `linearIndependent_int_of_zmod2` — independence mod 2 lifts to independence
  over `ℤ` (a 2-adic descent: a relation with all coefficients even halves).
* `rank_zmod2_le_rank_rat` — **one-sided error**: for every integer matrix,
  `rank_{𝔽₂} ≤ rank_ℚ`.  A `ℚ`-instrument can only *over*-report the `𝔽₂`-rank,
  hence only *under*-report the null space — exactly the failure mode in which a
  QS reports "no dependency yet" while one exists.
-/

namespace GF2RankTrap

open Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- Over a field, full rank is equivalent to a nonzero determinant. -/
theorem rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero {F : Type*} [Field F] (A : Matrix n n F) :
    A.rank = Fintype.card n ↔ A.det ≠ 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h hdet
    obtain ⟨v, hv0, hv⟩ := Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.2 hdet
    have htop : LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin = ⊤ := by
      apply Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq
      rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card]
      exact h
    have hsurj : Function.Surjective A.mulVecLin := LinearMap.range_eq_top.1 htop
    have hinj : Function.Injective A.mulVecLin :=
      LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective.2 hsurj
    apply hv0
    apply hinj
    simp [hv]
  · intro h
    exact A.rank_of_isUnit ((Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det A).2 (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 h))

/-- `𝔽₂`-full rank of an integer matrix is oddness of its determinant. -/
theorem rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n ↔ Odd A.det := by
  have hdet : (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).det = ((A.det : ℤ) : ZMod 2) := by
    rw [show A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) = (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)).mapMatrix A
      from rfl, ← RingHom.map_det]
    simp
  rw [rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero, hdet, ← Int.not_even_iff_odd, Ne,
    ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd, even_iff_two_dvd]
  norm_num

/-- `ℚ`-full rank of an integer matrix is nonvanishing of its determinant. -/
theorem rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n ↔ A.det ≠ 0 := by
  have hdet : (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).det = ((A.det : ℤ) : ℚ) := by
    rw [show A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = (Int.castRingHom ℚ).mapMatrix A
      from rfl, ← RingHom.map_det]
    simp
  rw [rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero, hdet]
  exact_mod_cast Iff.rfl

/-- **Discriminating-test criterion.**  The `ℚ`-instrument and the `𝔽₂`-instrument
agree on whether a square integer matrix has full rank *unless and only unless*
its determinant is a nonzero even integer. -/
theorem full_rank_agree_iff (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    ((A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n ↔
      (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n) ↔
      ¬ (A.det ≠ 0 ∧ Even A.det) := by
  rw [rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero, rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det, ← Int.not_even_iff_odd]
  by_cases h0 : A.det = 0
  · simp [h0]
  · by_cases he : Even A.det <;> simp [h0, he]

/-- The `𝔽₂`-rank of an integer matrix never exceeds the size, and is full only
when the `ℚ`-rank is full (a nonzero even determinant drops only the `𝔽₂`-rank). -/
theorem rat_full_of_zmod2_full (A : Matrix n n ℤ)
    (h : (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n := by
  rw [rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det] at h
  rw [rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero]
  rintro h0; rw [h0] at h; exact absurd h (by decide)

/-- Rank does not increase under taking an arbitrary submatrix. -/
theorem rank_submatrix_le_of_field {F : Type*} [Field F] {m k r : Type*}
    [Fintype m] [Fintype k] [Fintype r] (A : Matrix m m F) (f : k → m) (g : r → m) :
    (A.submatrix f g).rank ≤ A.rank := by
  have h1 : (A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m)).rank ≤ A.rank := rank_submatrix_le f _ A
  have h2 : ((A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.submatrix g (Equiv.refl k)).rank ≤
      (A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.rank := rank_submatrix_le g _ _
  have h3 : (A.submatrix f g) = ((A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.submatrix g
      (Equiv.refl k))ᵀ := by
    ext i j; rfl
  rw [h3, rank_transpose]
  rw [rank_transpose] at h2
  exact h2.trans h1

/-! ## The round-42 witness -/

/-- The `3 × 3` cycle-incidence matrix: rows are the edges of a triangle. -/
def trap3 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℤ := !![1, 1, 0; 0, 1, 1; 1, 0, 1]

theorem trap3_det : trap3.det = 2 := by
  simp [trap3, Matrix.det_fin_three]

/-- Over `ℚ` the witness has rank `3`. -/
theorem trap3_rank_rat : (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = 3 := by
  have := (rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero trap3).2 (by rw [trap3_det]; norm_num)
  simpa using this

/-- Over `𝔽₂` the same witness has rank `2` — the value a correct instrument
must return and a `ℚ`-instrument does not. -/
theorem trap3_rank_zmod2 : (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = 2 := by
  set A := trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) with hA
  have hlt : A.rank ≠ 3 := by
    intro h
    have h' : A.rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3) := by simpa using h
    rw [hA, rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det, trap3_det] at h'
    exact absurd h' (by decide)
  have hle : A.rank ≤ 3 := by simpa using A.rank_le_card_width
  have hsub : (A.submatrix (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
      (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))).rank = 2 := by
    have : (A.submatrix (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
        (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))).det ≠ 0 := by
      rw [Matrix.det_fin_two]
      simp [hA, trap3]
    simpa using (rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero _).2 this
  have hge := rank_submatrix_le_of_field A (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
    (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))
  omega

/-- The witness is discriminating, as the criterion predicts (`det = 2`). -/
theorem trap3_discriminates :
    ¬ ((trap3.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3) ↔
      (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3)) := by
  rw [full_rank_agree_iff, trap3_det]
  simp

/-! ## The error is one-sided -/

/-- Independence mod 2 lifts to independence over `ℤ`. -/
theorem linearIndependent_int_of_zmod2 {ι m : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (v : ι → m → ℤ)
    (h : LinearIndependent (ZMod 2) (fun i => fun k => ((v i k : ℤ) : ZMod 2))) :

/-!
# Round 42, open problem: large primes decouple yield from the column space

Round 42 closed with: *given a fixed `B`, can the yield collapse be evaded without
shrinking the column space?*  The first candidate channel listed is the
large-prime (partial-relation) variant.  This file proves the algebraic core of
that channel: partial relations sharing a large prime can be paired so that the
large prime cancels, and the resulting combined relations live in the **same**
`𝔽₂^Q` column space as the full relations.

Setting: `A` is the column set (the admissible primes, `|A| = Q`).
* `a` *full* relations `F j`, each nonzero with prime support in `A`;
* `b` *partial* relations `P i = s i * ℓ i` with `s i` nonzero, `A`-supported and
  `ℓ i` an arbitrary (large) prime;
* `D` = the number of **distinct** large primes among the partials.

Results:
* `lpRep` — for each partial, the canonical representative (least index) sharing
  its large prime; `lpRep_large` / `lpRep_idem`.
* `card_nonrep_ge` — at least `b - D` partials are not their own representative.
* `large_prime_congruence` — **if `Q < a + (b - D)`, some nonempty collection of
  full relations and paired partials `P i · P (lpRep i)` multiplies to a perfect
  square.**  The column count is still `Q`; the relation count grew from `a` to
  `a + b - D`.
* `combined_value_eq` — each pair is `s i · s (lpRep i) · ℓ i ²`: the large prime
  appears to an even power and so contributes no column.

So with partials the threshold for a guaranteed dependence is
`#full + #partials - #distinct large primes > Q`, with the column space untouched:
this is the precise sense in which the large-prime channel evades the yield
collapse "without shrinking the column space".  Whether it is *cheaper* is a
question about how fast `b - D` grows (a birthday-type collision count), not
about linear algebra.
-/

namespace QSLargePrime

open Finset

variable {b : ℕ}

/-- The canonical representative of the large-prime class of `i`: the least
index whose large prime coincides with that of `i`. -/
def lpRep (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) (i : Fin b) : Fin b :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => ℓ j = ℓ i)).min' ⟨i, by simp⟩

theorem lpRep_large (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) (i : Fin b) : ℓ (lpRep ℓ i) = ℓ i := by
  have := Finset.min'_mem (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => ℓ j = ℓ i)) ⟨i, by simp⟩
  simpa [lpRep] using this

/-- The representative depends only on the large prime. -/
theorem lpRep_congr (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) {i j : Fin b} (h : ℓ i = ℓ j) :
    lpRep ℓ i = lpRep ℓ j := by
  unfold lpRep
  congr 1
  ext k; simp [h]

theorem lpRep_idem (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) (i : Fin b) : lpRep ℓ (lpRep ℓ i) = lpRep ℓ i :=
  lpRep_congr ℓ (lpRep_large ℓ i)

/-- The fixed points of `lpRep` inject into the set of distinct large primes. -/
theorem card_rep_le (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => lpRep ℓ i = i)).card ≤ (Finset.univ.image ℓ).card := by
  apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn ℓ
  · intro i _; simp
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hi hj
    rw [← hi, ← hj]
    exact lpRep_congr ℓ hij

/-- At least `b - D` partials are *paired* (not their own representative). -/
theorem card_nonrep_ge (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) :
    b - (Finset.univ.image ℓ).card ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => lpRep ℓ i ≠ i)).card := by
  have h1 := card_rep_le ℓ
  have h2 := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin b)))
    (fun i => lpRep ℓ i = i)
  simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h2
  simp only [ne_eq]
  omega

/-- A paired partial relation is `s i · s (lpRep i) · (ℓ i)²`. -/
theorem combined_value_eq (s ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) (i : Fin b) :
    (s i * ℓ i) * (s (lpRep ℓ i) * ℓ (lpRep ℓ i)) = (s i * s (lpRep ℓ i)) * ℓ i ^ 2 := by
  rw [lpRep_large ℓ i]; ring

/-- The combined relation set: full relations, plus paired partials. -/
abbrev CombIdx (a : ℕ) (ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) :=
  Fin a ⊕ {i : Fin b // lpRep ℓ i ≠ i}

/-- The value of a combined relation. -/
def combValue {a : ℕ} (F : Fin a → ℕ) (s ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) : CombIdx a ℓ → ℕ
  | Sum.inl j => F j
  | Sum.inr i => (s i.1 * ℓ i.1) * (s (lpRep ℓ i.1) * ℓ (lpRep ℓ i.1))

/-- Its `A`-part, with the squared large prime removed. -/
def combCore {a : ℕ} (F : Fin a → ℕ) (s ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) : CombIdx a ℓ → ℕ
  | Sum.inl j => F j
  | Sum.inr i => s i.1 * s (lpRep ℓ i.1)

/-- **Large-prime congruence of squares.**  If the number of full relations plus
the number of paired partials exceeds the column count `Q = |A|`, some nonempty
collection of combined relations multiplies to a perfect square.  The column
space is the same `𝔽₂^A` as for full relations alone. -/
theorem large_prime_congruence {a : ℕ} (A : Finset ℕ)
    (F : Fin a → ℕ) (hF0 : ∀ j, F j ≠ 0) (hFA : ∀ j, (F j).primeFactors ⊆ A)
    (s ℓ : Fin b → ℕ) (hs0 : ∀ i, s i ≠ 0) (hsA : ∀ i, (s i).primeFactors ⊆ A)
    (hQ : A.card < a + (b - (Finset.univ.image ℓ).card)) :
    ∃ T : Finset (CombIdx a ℓ), T.Nonempty ∧ IsSquare (∏ t ∈ T, combValue F s ℓ t) := by
  classical
  have hcore0 : ∀ t, combCore F s ℓ t ≠ 0 := by
    rintro (j | i)
    · exact hF0 j
    · exact Nat.mul_ne_zero (hs0 _) (hs0 _)
  have hcoreA : ∀ t, ∀ p, (combCore F s ℓ t).factorization p ≠ 0 → p ∈ A := by
    intro t p hp
    have hmem : p ∈ (combCore F s ℓ t).primeFactors := by
      rw [← Nat.support_factorization]; exact Finsupp.mem_support_iff.2 hp
    rcases t with j | i
    · exact hFA j hmem
    · simp only [combCore] at hmem
      rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul (hs0 _) (hs0 _)] at hmem
      rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hmem with h | h
      · exact hsA _ h
      · exact hsA _ h
  have hcard : A.card < Fintype.card (CombIdx a ℓ) := by
    rw [Fintype.card_sum, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_subtype]
    have := card_nonrep_ge ℓ
    simp only [ne_eq] at this ⊢
    omega
  obtain ⟨T, hTne, hsq⟩ :=
    QSDimension.exists_nonempty_subset_prod_isSquare A (combCore F s ℓ) hcore0 hcoreA hcard
  refine ⟨T, hTne, ?_⟩
  have hsplit : ∀ t, combValue F s ℓ t = combCore F s ℓ t *
      (match t with | Sum.inl _ => 1 | Sum.inr i => ℓ i.1) ^ 2 := by
    rintro (j | i)
    · simp [combValue, combCore]
    · simp only [combValue, combCore]; exact combined_value_eq s ℓ i.1
  rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun t _ => hsplit t), Finset.prod_mul_distrib,
    Finset.prod_pow]
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hsq
  exact ⟨r * ∏ t ∈ T, (match t with | Sum.inl _ => 1 | Sum.inr i => ℓ i.1), by rw [hr]; ring⟩

/-! ## Lab notes

`A = {2, 3}` (`Q = 2`), one full relation `F₀ = 6`, and three partials sharing
the large prime `101`: `P = 2·101, 3·101, 6·101` (`a = 1`, `b = 3`, `D = 1`).
The threshold `Q = 2 < a + (b - D) = 3` holds.  Pairing with the representative
(index `0`) gives `P₁P₀ = 6·101²` and `P₂P₀ = 12·101²`; the full relation and the
first pair already multiply to a square, `6 · (3·101)(2·101) = (6·101)²`.  Without
the partials (`a = 1 ≤ Q`) no dependence is guaranteed. -/

example : (6 : ℕ) * ((3 * 101) * (2 * 101)) = (6 * 101) * (6 * 101) := by norm_num

end QSLargePrime

namespace QSSplitForcing

open Finset QSDimension QSRelationPool SmoothSparsity

/-- **Sieve divisibility forces a split prime.**  If a prime `r` with `r ∤ N`
divides a sieve value `x² - N`, then `(N / r) = +1`. -/
theorem legendreSym_eq_one_of_dvd_qsValue {r : ℕ} [Fact r.Prime] {N x : ℤ}
    (hdvd : (r : ℤ) ∣ qsValue N x) (hN : ¬ (r : ℤ) ∣ N) :
    legendreSym r N = 1 := by
  have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
    rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
  exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).2 (isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue hdvd)

open Classical in
/-- The *sieve-reachable* primes: primes `≤ B` dividing at least one value
`x² - N`.  This is the set of columns a single-polynomial sieve can ever touch. -/
noncomputable def sieveReachable (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (factorBase B).filter (fun p => ∃ x : ℤ, (p : ℤ) ∣ qsValue N x)

/-- **The factor base is the split set.**  The primes hit by the sieve are
exactly the admissible primes. -/
theorem sieveReachable_eq_admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    sieveReachable N B = admissiblePrimes N B := by
  classical
  ext p
  simp only [sieveReachable, admissiblePrimes, Finset.mem_filter]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hp, x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨hp, isSquare_of_dvd_qsValue hx⟩
  · rintro ⟨hp, hsq⟩
    have hpr : p.Prime := (mem_factorBase.1 hp).1
    haveI : NeZero p := ⟨hpr.ne_zero⟩
    exact ⟨hp, (exists_dvd_qsValue_iff_isSquare N).2 hsq⟩

open Classical in
/-- **Ramified ∪ split decomposition.**  The admissible primes are exactly the
primes `r ≤ B` with `r ∣ N` together with those with `(N / r) = +1`. -/
theorem admissiblePrimes_eq_ramified_union_split (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    admissiblePrimes N B =
      (factorBase B).filter (fun r : ℕ => (r : ℤ) ∣ N) ∪
      (factorBase B).filter (fun r : ℕ => ∃ h : r.Prime,
        @legendreSym r ⟨h⟩ N = 1) := by
  ext r
  simp only [admissiblePrimes, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_filter]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hr, hsq⟩
    have hpr : r.Prime := (mem_factorBase.1 hr).1
    haveI : Fact r.Prime := ⟨hpr⟩
    by_cases hN : (r : ℤ) ∣ N
    · exact Or.inl ⟨hr, hN⟩
    · refine Or.inr ⟨hr, hpr, ?_⟩
      have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
        rwa [Ne, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]
      exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).2 hsq
  · rintro (⟨hr, hN⟩ | ⟨hr, hpr, hleg⟩)
    · refine ⟨hr, ⟨0, ?_⟩⟩
      rw [(ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd N r).2 hN]; ring
    · haveI : Fact r.Prime := ⟨hpr⟩
      refine ⟨hr, ?_⟩
      have hne : ((N : ZMod r)) ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0
        have : legendreSym r N = 0 := (legendreSym.eq_zero_iff r N).2 h0
        rw [this] at hleg; exact absurd hleg (by norm_num)
      exact (legendreSym.eq_one_iff r hne).1 hleg

/-- **Smoothness of a sieve value is smoothness over the split set.**  For a
sieve value `v = x² - N`, being `B`-smooth is equivalent to having its
whole prime support inside the admissible set. -/
theorem qs_smooth_iff_admissible_support {B : ℕ} {N x : ℤ} {v : ℕ}
    (hval : (v : ℤ) = x ^ 2 - N) :
    (∀ p ∈ v.primeFactors, p ≤ B) ↔ v.primeFactors ⊆ admissiblePrimes N B := by
  constructor
  · intro hsm p hp
    have hfac : v.factorization p ≠ 0 := by
      rw [← Finsupp.mem_support_iff, Nat.support_factorization]; exact hp
    exact smooth_qsValue_support hval hsm p hfac
  · intro hsub p hp
    exact (mem_factorBase.1 (admissiblePrimes_subset N B (hsub hp))).2

open Classical in
/-- `Q(N,B) ≤ π(B)`, with the deficit counted exactly by the primes that are
neither ramified nor split (the inert primes). -/
theorem admissible_card_add_inert (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    (admissiblePrimes N B).card +
      ((factorBase B).filter (fun p => ¬ IsSquare ((N : ZMod p)))).card =
      (factorBase B).card := by
  classical
  unfold admissiblePrimes
  exact Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _

theorem admissible_card_le_factorBase (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ) :
    (admissiblePrimes N B).card ≤ (factorBase B).card :=
  Finset.card_le_card (admissiblePrimes_subset N B)

import Mathlib
import Computation.QSSplitSetForcing

/-!
# Round 42, items 1–2: the smooth yield is governed by `Q`, not by `π(B)` alone

Round 42 measured that, at matched `u = log X / log B`, the sieve's smooth density
is essentially uncorrelated with `ρ(u)` (`+0.029`) and strongly correlated with
`Q/π(B)` (`+0.882`), and that paid sieve work *decreases* as `Q` grows.  This file
proves the unconditional skeleton of both observations.

**Smooth counting over an arbitrary prime set.**  `psiS S X` counts `n ∈ [1, X]`
whose prime support lies in `S` (so `psiS (factorBase B) X = Ψ(X, B)`).

* `psiS_mono` — `psiS` is monotone in the prime set.
* `psiS_insert_ge` — **the multiplicative step**: adjoining a new prime `p`
  gives `Ψ_{S∪{p}}(X) ≥ Ψ_S(X) + Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋)`.
* `two_pow_card_le_psiS` — **exponential floor**: if `∏ S ≤ X` then
  `2^{|S|} ≤ Ψ_S(X)` (all square-free sub-products).
* `psiS_le_pow_card` — **exponential ceiling**: `Ψ_S(X) ≤ (log₂ X + 1)^{|S|}`.

So at a fixed value size `X` (fixed `u`), the count is squeezed between two
functions that are exponential in `|S|` — the *exponent* is the size of the
prime set, and nothing else about `B` enters.

**Specialisation to the sieve.**

* `qsYield_le_psiS_admissible` / `qsYield_le_pow_Q` — the number of `B`-smooth
  sieve values `x² - N` on a window `[a, b]` (with `a² > N`) is at most
  `Ψ_{A}(b² - N) ≤ (log₂(b² - N) + 1)^{Q(N,B)}`: the ceiling is governed by
  `Q(N,B)`, the split-set size, *not* by `π(B)`.  Two moduli with the same `B` and
  the same window (hence the same `u`) can therefore have yield ceilings differing
  by the factor `(log₂ X + 1)^{π(B)(Q₁/π(B) - Q₂/π(B))}` — this is the formal
  shadow of "Dickman is blind to `Q`".

**The sign-flip criterion.**

* `work_mono_iff` — in the cost model `work(S) = (|S| + 1) / Ψ_S(X)` (positions
  per guaranteed dependence at fixed `X`), adjoining a prime lowers the work iff
  `(|S| + 1)(Ψ_{S∪{p}} - Ψ_S) ≥ Ψ_S`.
* `work_decreases_of_marginal` — the multiplicative step makes this hold as soon
  as `(|S| + 1) · Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋) ≥ Ψ_S(X)`: one more column is paid for by the
  additive `+1` in the relation target, while it buys a *multiplicative* gain in
  the smooth count.  This is the structural reason why "shrinking `Q` to shrink
  the linear algebra moves the wrong term".
-/

namespace QSSplitYield

open Finset

/-- `Ψ_S(X)`: the number of `n ∈ [1, X]` all of whose prime factors lie in `S`. -/
def psiS (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S)).card

theorem psiS_mono {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : S ⊆ T) (X : ℕ) : psiS S X ≤ psiS T X := by
  unfold psiS
  apply Finset.card_le_card
  intro n hn
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hn ⊢
  exact ⟨hn.1, hn.2.trans h⟩

/-- `psiS` over the factor base is the classical `Ψ(X, B)` of the catalog. -/
theorem psiS_factorBase (B X : ℕ) :
    psiS (SmoothSparsity.factorBase B) X = (SmoothSparsity.smoothPool B X).card := by
  unfold psiS SmoothSparsity.smoothPool
  congr 1
  apply Finset.filter_congr
  intro n _
  constructor
  · intro h p hp; exact (SmoothSparsity.mem_factorBase.1 (h hp)).2
  · intro h p hp
    exact SmoothSparsity.mem_factorBase.2 ⟨Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp, h p hp⟩

/-- **The multiplicative step.**  Adjoining a new prime `p ∉ S` adds at least
`Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋)` new smooth numbers (namely `p · m`). -/
theorem psiS_insert_ge {S : Finset ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpS : p ∉ S) (X : ℕ) :
    psiS S X + psiS S (X / p) ≤ psiS (insert p S) X := by
  classical
  set A := (Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S) with hA
  set C := (Finset.Icc 1 (X / p)).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S) with hC
  set D := (Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ insert p S) with hD
  have hp0 : 0 < p := hp.pos
  have hCimg : C.image (fun m => p * m) ⊆ D := by
    intro n hn
    obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hn
    simp only [hC, hD, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hm ⊢
    have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by omega
    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (Nat.mul_ne_zero hp.ne_zero hm0)
    · have := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hp0).1 hm.1.2
      linarith [mul_comm m p]
    · rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul hp.ne_zero hm0, hp.primeFactors]
      exact Finset.union_subset (by simp) (hm.2.trans (Finset.subset_insert _ _))
  have hAD : A ⊆ D := by
    intro n hn
    simp only [hA, hD, Finset.mem_filter] at hn ⊢
    exact ⟨hn.1, hn.2.trans (Finset.subset_insert _ _)⟩
  have hdisj : Disjoint A (C.image (fun m => p * m)) := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro n hnA hnC
    obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hnC
    simp only [hA, hC, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hnA hm
    have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by omega
    apply hpS
    apply hnA.2
    rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul hp.ne_zero hm0, hp.primeFactors]
    simp
  have hcardC : (C.image (fun m => p * m)).card = C.card :=
    Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun a b h => Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hp0 h)
  have := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.union_subset hAD hCimg)
  rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, hcardC] at this
  exact this

/-- **Exponential floor.**  If every element of `S` is prime and `∏ S ≤ X`, then
`2^{|S|} ≤ Ψ_S(X)`: the `2^{|S|}` square-free sub-products are distinct and
`S`-smooth. -/
theorem two_pow_card_le_psiS {S : Finset ℕ} (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime) {X : ℕ}
    (hX : ∏ p ∈ S, p ≤ X) : 2 ^ S.card ≤ psiS S X := by
  classical
  rw [← Finset.card_powerset]
  unfold psiS
  refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun T => ∏ p ∈ T, p) ?_ ?_
  · intro T hT
    have hTS : T ⊆ S := Finset.mem_powerset.1 hT
    have hTp : ∀ p ∈ T, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (hTS hp)
    dsimp only
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc]
    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2
        (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.2 (fun p hp => (hTp p hp).ne_zero))
    · refine le_trans ?_ hX
      exact Finset.prod_le_prod_of_subset_of_one_le' hTS
        (fun i hi _ => (hS i hi).one_lt.le)
    · rw [Nat.primeFactors_prod hTp]; exact hTS
  · intro T hT U hU hTU
    have hTp : ∀ p ∈ T, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (Finset.mem_powerset.1 hT hp)
    have hUp : ∀ p ∈ U, p.Prime := fun p hp => hS p (Finset.mem_powerset.1 hU hp)
    have := congrArg Nat.primeFactors hTU
    simp only at this
    rwa [Nat.primeFactors_prod hTp, Nat.primeFactors_prod hUp] at this

/-- **Exponential ceiling.**  `Ψ_S(X) ≤ (log₂ X + 1)^{|S|}`. -/
theorem psiS_le_pow_card (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) :
    psiS S X ≤ (Nat.log 2 X + 1) ^ S.card := by
  classical
  set k := Nat.log 2 X with hk
  set f : ℕ → (S → Fin (k + 1)) :=
    fun n p => ⟨min (n.factorization p) k, by omega⟩ with hf
  have hinj : Set.InjOn f ((Finset.Icc 1 X).filter (fun n => n.primeFactors ⊆ S)) := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha hb
    have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hb0 : b ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hfa : ∀ p, a.factorization p = b.factorization p := by
      intro p
      by_cases hp : p ∈ S
      · have := congrFun hab ⟨p, hp⟩
        simp only [hf, Fin.mk.injEq] at this
        have h1 := SmoothSparsity.factorization_le_log_two (p := p) ha0 ha.1.2
        have h2 := SmoothSparsity.factorization_le_log_two (p := p) hb0 hb.1.2
        omega
      · have hA : a.factorization p = 0 := by
          by_contra hcon
          exact hp (ha.2 (by rw [← Nat.support_factorization]; exact Finsupp.mem_support_iff.2 hcon))
        have hB : b.factorization p = 0 := by
          by_contra hcon
          exact hp (hb.2 (by rw [← Nat.support_factorization]; exact Finsupp.mem_support_iff.2 hcon))
        rw [hA, hB]
    exact Nat.factorization_inj ha0 hb0 (Finsupp.ext hfa)
  unfold psiS
  calc _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (S → Fin (k + 1))).card :=
        Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn f (fun n _ => Finset.mem_univ _) hinj
    _ = (k + 1) ^ S.card := by simp

/-! ## The sieve yield is bounded by a function of `Q(N,B)` -/

/-- The number of sieve positions `x ∈ [a, b]` whose value `x² - N` is
`B`-smooth. -/
def qsYield (N B a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc a b).filter (fun x => ∀ p ∈ (x ^ 2 - N).primeFactors, p ≤ B)).card

/-- **Yield ceiling by the split set.**  On a window `[a, b]` with `N < a²`, the
`B`-smooth yield is at most `Ψ_{A(N,B)}(b² - N)`. -/
theorem qsYield_le_psiS_admissible (N B a b : ℕ) (ha : N < a ^ 2) :
    qsYield N B a b ≤ psiS (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) B) (b ^ 2 - N) := by
  classical
  unfold qsYield psiS
  refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun x => x ^ 2 - N) ?_ ?_
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx
    obtain ⟨⟨hax, hxb⟩, hsm⟩ := hx
    have hxa : a ^ 2 ≤ x ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hax 2
    have hxb2 : x ^ 2 ≤ b ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hxb 2
    dsimp only
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc]
    refine ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
    have hval : ((x ^ 2 - N : ℕ) : ℤ) = (x : ℤ) ^ 2 - (N : ℤ) := by
      push_cast [show N ≤ x ^ 2 by omega]; ring
    exact (QSSplitForcing.qs_smooth_iff_admissible_support hval).1 hsm
  · intro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx hy hxy
    have hx2 : a ^ 2 ≤ x ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hx.1.1 2
    have hy2 : a ^ 2 ≤ y ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hy.1.1 2
    have : x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 := by omega
    exact Nat.pow_left_injective (by norm_num) this

/-- **The yield ceiling depends on `Q`, not on `π(B)`.** -/
theorem qsYield_le_pow_Q (N B a b : ℕ) (ha : N < a ^ 2) :
    qsYield N B a b ≤
      (Nat.log 2 (b ^ 2 - N) + 1) ^ (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes (N : ℤ) B).card :=
  (qsYield_le_psiS_admissible N B a b ha).trans (psiS_le_pow_card _ _)

/-! ## The sign-flip criterion -/

/-- Model cost: positions per guaranteed dependence, `(|S| + 1) / Ψ_S(X)`. -/
noncomputable def work (S : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) : ℚ := ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) / (psiS S X : ℚ)

/-- **Criterion.**  For `p ∉ S` with `Ψ_S(X) > 0`, adjoining `p` does not raise
the model work iff `(|S| + 1)(Ψ_{S∪{p}} - Ψ_S) ≥ Ψ_S`. -/
theorem work_mono_iff {S : Finset ℕ} {p X : ℕ} (hpS : p ∉ S)
    (hpos : 0 < psiS S X) (hpos' : 0 < psiS (insert p S) X) :
    work (insert p S) X ≤ work S X ↔
      (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * ((psiS (insert p S) X : ℚ) - psiS S X) := by
  unfold work
  rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hpS, div_le_div_iff₀ (by exact_mod_cast hpos')
    (by exact_mod_cast hpos)]
  push_cast
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/-- **The sign flip.**  If the marginal prime satisfies
`(|S| + 1) · Ψ_S(⌊X/p⌋) ≥ Ψ_S(X)`, then adjoining it (raising `Q` by one) does not
increase the model work. -/
theorem work_decreases_of_marginal {S : Finset ℕ} {p X : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpS : p ∉ S)
    (hpos : 0 < psiS S X) (hmarg : psiS S X ≤ (S.card + 1) * psiS S (X / p)) :
    work (insert p S) X ≤ work S X := by
  have hstep := psiS_insert_ge hp hpS X
  have hpos' : 0 < psiS (insert p S) X := by omega
  rw [work_mono_iff hpS hpos hpos']
  have h1 : (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) := by
    exact_mod_cast hmarg
  have h2 : (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) ≤ (psiS (insert p S) X : ℚ) - psiS S X := by
    have : ((psiS S X + psiS S (X / p) : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ psiS (insert p S) X := by
      exact_mod_cast hstep
    push_cast at this; linarith
  calc (psiS S X : ℚ) ≤ ((S.card : ℚ) + 1) * (psiS S (X / p) : ℚ) := h1
    _ ≤ _ := by
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2; positivity

/-! ## Lab notes: an explicit sign flip

`S = {2, 3}`, `X = 100`, `p = 5`.  `Ψ_{2,3}(100) = 20`, `Ψ_{2,3}(20) = 10`, so
the marginal condition `3 · 10 ≥ 20` holds and
`work({2,3,5}) = 4/34 < 3/20 = work({2,3})` (indeed `Ψ_{2,3,5}(100) = 34`). -/

theorem lab_psi23_100 : psiS {2, 3} 100 = 20 := by native_decide
theorem lab_psi23_20 : psiS {2, 3} (100 / 5) = 10 := by native_decide
theorem lab_psi235_100 : psiS {5, 2, 3} 100 = 34 := by native_decide

/-- The marginal criterion certifies the flip without computing `Ψ_{2,3,5}`. -/
example : work (insert 5 {2, 3}) 100 ≤ work {2, 3} 100 :=
  work_decreases_of_marginal (by norm_num) (by decide) (by rw [lab_psi23_100]; norm_num)
    (by rw [lab_psi23_100, lab_psi23_20]; decide)

/-- And the strict inequality from the measured counts. -/
example : work (insert 5 {2, 3}) 100 < work {2, 3} 100 := by
  unfold work
  rw [show (insert 5 {2, 3} : Finset ℕ) = {5, 2, 3} from rfl, lab_psi235_100, lab_psi23_100]
  norm_num

end QSSplitYield

/-!
# Round 42, item 4: which way does `rank ≤ Q` point?  The prefix-rank identity

The sieve produces relation (exponent) vectors `v₀, v₁, v₂, …` in `𝔽₂^Q`, where
`Q = Q(N,B)` is the number of admissible primes (`Catalog.Computation.QSSplitSetForcing`).
`k_success` is the length of the *shortest* prefix that is linearly dependent.
Round 42 asserted that the chain `k_success ≤ rank + 1 ≤ Q + 1` "has its first
inequality backwards".  This file settles the question exactly, over any field,
and finds that **both readings are right about different ranks**:

* `prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent` — for any dependent prefix of length `k`,
  `rank(prefix k) + 1 ≤ k` (round 42's correction, for the *prefix* rank);
* `kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one` — the **identity**
  `k_success = rank(prefix k_success) + 1`: at the first dependence the two sides
  meet;
* `kSuccess_le_rank_add_one` — for every collected matrix `M = prefix n` with
  `n ≥ k_success`, `k_success ≤ rank(M) + 1` (so the original chain is *true* when
  `rank` means the rank of all relations collected);
* `kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one` — `k_success ≤ Q + 1`;
* `kSuccess_basis` — the bound `Q + 1` is attained (standard basis first), so the
  empirical ratios `k_success/Q ≈ 0.78/0.71/0.60` are properties of the instances,
  not of the algebra.

The bound counts **relations**, not sieve positions: nothing here bounds the
paid work, which is the number of positions needed to *find* `k_success`
relations.
-/

namespace QSPrefixRank

open Module

variable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]

/-- The first `k` relation vectors, as a family indexed by `Fin k`. -/
def pre (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : Fin k → V := fun i => v i

/-- Rank of the first `k` relation vectors. -/
noncomputable def prefixRank (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Set.finrank K (Set.range (pre v k))

omit [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] in
theorem range_pre_mono (v : ℕ → V) {k m : ℕ} (h : k ≤ m) :
    Set.range (pre v k) ⊆ Set.range (pre v m) := by
  rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨⟨i, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 h⟩, rfl⟩

theorem prefixRank_le (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) : prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ k := by
  have := finrank_range_le_card (R := K) (pre v k)
  simpa [prefixRank] using this

theorem prefixRank_mono (v : ℕ → V) {k m : ℕ} (h : k ≤ m) :
    prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ prefixRank (K := K) v m := by
  unfold prefixRank Set.finrank
  haveI : FiniteDimensional K (Submodule.span K (Set.range (pre v m))) :=
    FiniteDimensional.span_of_finite K (Set.finite_range _)
  exact Submodule.finrank_mono (Submodule.span_mono (range_pre_mono v h))

/-- Independence of a prefix is exactly "rank = length". -/
theorem linearIndependent_pre_iff (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) :
    LinearIndependent K (pre v k) ↔ prefixRank (K := K) v k = k := by
  rw [linearIndependent_iff_card_eq_finrank_span, Fintype.card_fin, prefixRank]
  exact eq_comm

/-- **Round 42's direction correction.**  A dependence at prefix `k` forces
`rank(prefix k) + 1 ≤ k`. -/
theorem prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (h : ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k)) : prefixRank (K := K) v k + 1 ≤ k := by
  rw [linearIndependent_pre_iff] at h
  have := prefixRank_le (K := K) v k
  omega

/-- More than `dim V` relations are always dependent. -/
theorem dependent_of_finrank_lt [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : finrank K V < k) : ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k) := by
  intro hli
  have := hli.fintype_card_le_finrank
  rw [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

theorem exists_dependent [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    ∃ k, ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v k) :=
  ⟨finrank K V + 1, dependent_of_finrank_lt v (Nat.lt_succ_self _)⟩

open Classical in
/-- `k_success`: the length of the shortest dependent prefix. -/
noncomputable def kSuccess [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) : ℕ :=
  Nat.find (exists_dependent (K := K) v)

theorem kSuccess_dependent [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    ¬ LinearIndependent K (pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v)) := by
  classical
  exact Nat.find_spec (exists_dependent (K := K) v)

theorem independent_of_lt_kSuccess [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < kSuccess (K := K) v) : LinearIndependent K (pre v k) := by
  classical
  by_contra h
  exact Nat.find_min (exists_dependent (K := K) v) hk h

theorem kSuccess_pos [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) : 0 < kSuccess (K := K) v := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (kSuccess (K := K) v) with h | h
  · have hd := kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v
    rw [h] at hd
    exact absurd (linearIndependent_empty_type) hd
  · exact h

/-- **The prefix-rank identity.**  `k_success = rank(prefix k_success) + 1`. -/
theorem kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v = prefixRank (K := K) v (kSuccess (K := K) v) + 1 := by
  set k := kSuccess (K := K) v with hk
  have hpos : 0 < k := kSuccess_pos (K := K) v
  have hup : prefixRank (K := K) v k + 1 ≤ k :=
    prefixRank_add_one_le_of_dependent v (kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v)
  have hind : LinearIndependent K (pre v (k - 1)) :=
    independent_of_lt_kSuccess v (by omega)
  have hr : prefixRank (K := K) v (k - 1) = k - 1 := (linearIndependent_pre_iff v _).1 hind
  have hmono := prefixRank_mono (K := K) v (Nat.sub_le k 1)
  omega

/-- **The original chain, for the full collected matrix.**  If `n ≥ k_success`
relations have been collected, `k_success ≤ rank(M) + 1` where `M = prefix n`. -/
theorem kSuccess_le_rank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ n) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ prefixRank (K := K) v n + 1 := by
  have h1 := kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one (K := K) v
  have h2 := prefixRank_mono (K := K) v hn
  omega

theorem prefixRank_le_finrank [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) (k : ℕ) :
    prefixRank (K := K) v k ≤ finrank K V := by
  unfold prefixRank Set.finrank
  exact Submodule.finrank_le _

/-- `k_success ≤ Q + 1` with `Q = dim V`. -/
theorem kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one [FiniteDimensional K V] (v : ℕ → V) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v ≤ finrank K V + 1 := by
  have h1 := kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one (K := K) v
  have h2 := prefixRank_le_finrank (K := K) v (kSuccess (K := K) v)
  omega

/-- **Sharpness.**  In `K^Q`, if the first `Q` relations are the standard basis,
then `k_success = Q + 1`. -/
theorem kSuccess_basis (Q : ℕ) (v : ℕ → (Fin Q → K))
    (hv : ∀ i : Fin Q, v i = Pi.single i 1) :
    kSuccess (K := K) v = Q + 1 := by
  have hle := kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one (K := K) v
  rw [finrank_fin_fun] at hle
  have hind : LinearIndependent K (pre v Q) := by
    have : pre v Q = fun i : Fin Q => (Pi.basisFun K (Fin Q)) i := by
      funext i; simp [pre, hv i]
    rw [this]; exact (Pi.basisFun K (Fin Q)).linearIndependent
  by_contra hne
  have hlt : Q < kSuccess (K := K) v := by
    by_contra hge
    push_neg at hge
    have hdep := kSuccess_dependent (K := K) v
    have hsub : LinearIndependent K (pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v)) := by
      have hcomp : pre v (kSuccess (K := K) v) =
          pre v Q ∘ Fin.castLE hge := by funext i; rfl
      rw [hcomp]; exact hind.comp _ (Fin.castLE_injective hge)
    exact hdep hsub
  omega

/-! ## Specialisation to the quadratic sieve: `Q(N,B) + 1` relations -/

/-- **QS form.**  For relation vectors in `𝔽₂^{A}`, `A` the admissible primes of
`N` at bound `B`, the first dependence occurs after at most `Q(N,B) + 1`
relations, and exactly one more than the rank of the prefix it closes. -/
theorem qs_kSuccess_bounds (N : ℤ) (B : ℕ)
    (v : ℕ → (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes N B → ZMod 2)) :
    kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v = prefixRank (K := ZMod 2) v (kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v) + 1 ∧
    kSuccess (K := ZMod 2) v ≤ (QSDimension.admissiblePrimes N B).card + 1 := by
  refine ⟨kSuccess_eq_prefixRank_add_one v, ?_⟩
  have := kSuccess_le_finrank_add_one (K := ZMod 2) v
  rwa [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, Fintype.card_coe] at this

end QSPrefixRank

import Mathlib

/-!
# Round 42, item 6: the `𝔽₂`-rank trap, and which test matrices can catch it

Round 42 found that two library routines silently returned the rank over `ℚ`
when asked for the rank over `GF(2)` (returning `3` on a matrix of `𝔽₂`-rank `2`),
and that "validation passed" was unfalsifiable until a mutation test was added.
This file makes both observations exact.

* `rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero` — over any field, a square matrix has full rank
  iff its determinant is nonzero.
* `rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det` / `rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero` — for an
  integer matrix `A`, full `𝔽₂`-rank ⇔ `det A` odd; full `ℚ`-rank ⇔ `det A ≠ 0`.
* `full_rank_agree_iff` — **the discriminating-test criterion**: a square integer
  test matrix can distinguish a "rank over `ℚ`" instrument from a correct
  "rank over `𝔽₂`" one *on the full-rank question* iff `det A` is a **nonzero even**
  integer.  A validation suite built from matrices with odd (or zero) determinant
  is blind to the bug, which is why the bug survived inspection.
* `trap3_rank_rat` / `trap3_rank_zmod2` — the round-42 witness: the `3 × 3`
  cycle-incidence matrix has `ℚ`-rank `3` and `𝔽₂`-rank `2`.
* `rank_submatrix_le_of_field` — rank does not increase under taking an arbitrary
  submatrix (rows and columns), the tool used for the lower bound.
* `linearIndependent_int_of_zmod2` — independence mod 2 lifts to independence
  over `ℤ` (a 2-adic descent: a relation with all coefficients even halves).
* `rank_zmod2_le_rank_rat` — **one-sided error**: for every integer matrix,
  `rank_{𝔽₂} ≤ rank_ℚ`.  A `ℚ`-instrument can only *over*-report the `𝔽₂`-rank,
  hence only *under*-report the null space — exactly the failure mode in which a
  QS reports "no dependency yet" while one exists.
-/

namespace GF2RankTrap

open Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- Over a field, full rank is equivalent to a nonzero determinant. -/
theorem rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero {F : Type*} [Field F] (A : Matrix n n F) :
    A.rank = Fintype.card n ↔ A.det ≠ 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h hdet
    obtain ⟨v, hv0, hv⟩ := Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.2 hdet
    have htop : LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin = ⊤ := by
      apply Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq
      rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card]
      exact h
    have hsurj : Function.Surjective A.mulVecLin := LinearMap.range_eq_top.1 htop
    have hinj : Function.Injective A.mulVecLin :=
      LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective.2 hsurj
    apply hv0
    apply hinj
    simp [hv]
  · intro h
    exact A.rank_of_isUnit ((Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det A).2 (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 h))

/-- `𝔽₂`-full rank of an integer matrix is oddness of its determinant. -/
theorem rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n ↔ Odd A.det := by
  have hdet : (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).det = ((A.det : ℤ) : ZMod 2) := by
    rw [show A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) = (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)).mapMatrix A
      from rfl, ← RingHom.map_det]
    simp
  rw [rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero, hdet, ← Int.not_even_iff_odd, Ne,
    ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd, even_iff_two_dvd]
  norm_num

/-- `ℚ`-full rank of an integer matrix is nonvanishing of its determinant. -/
theorem rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n ↔ A.det ≠ 0 := by
  have hdet : (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).det = ((A.det : ℤ) : ℚ) := by
    rw [show A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = (Int.castRingHom ℚ).mapMatrix A
      from rfl, ← RingHom.map_det]
    simp
  rw [rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero, hdet]
  exact_mod_cast Iff.rfl

/-- **Discriminating-test criterion.**  The `ℚ`-instrument and the `𝔽₂`-instrument
agree on whether a square integer matrix has full rank *unless and only unless*
its determinant is a nonzero even integer. -/
theorem full_rank_agree_iff (A : Matrix n n ℤ) :
    ((A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n ↔
      (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n) ↔
      ¬ (A.det ≠ 0 ∧ Even A.det) := by
  rw [rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero, rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det, ← Int.not_even_iff_odd]
  by_cases h0 : A.det = 0
  · simp [h0]
  · by_cases he : Even A.det <;> simp [h0, he]

/-- The `𝔽₂`-rank of an integer matrix never exceeds the size, and is full only
when the `ℚ`-rank is full (a nonzero even determinant drops only the `𝔽₂`-rank). -/
theorem rat_full_of_zmod2_full (A : Matrix n n ℤ)
    (h : (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card n) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card n := by
  rw [rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det] at h
  rw [rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero]
  rintro h0; rw [h0] at h; exact absurd h (by decide)

/-- Rank does not increase under taking an arbitrary submatrix. -/
theorem rank_submatrix_le_of_field {F : Type*} [Field F] {m k r : Type*}
    [Fintype m] [Fintype k] [Fintype r] (A : Matrix m m F) (f : k → m) (g : r → m) :
    (A.submatrix f g).rank ≤ A.rank := by
  have h1 : (A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m)).rank ≤ A.rank := rank_submatrix_le f _ A
  have h2 : ((A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.submatrix g (Equiv.refl k)).rank ≤
      (A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.rank := rank_submatrix_le g _ _
  have h3 : (A.submatrix f g) = ((A.submatrix f (Equiv.refl m))ᵀ.submatrix g
      (Equiv.refl k))ᵀ := by
    ext i j; rfl
  rw [h3, rank_transpose]
  rw [rank_transpose] at h2
  exact h2.trans h1

/-! ## The round-42 witness -/

/-- The `3 × 3` cycle-incidence matrix: rows are the edges of a triangle. -/
def trap3 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℤ := !![1, 1, 0; 0, 1, 1; 1, 0, 1]

theorem trap3_det : trap3.det = 2 := by
  simp [trap3, Matrix.det_fin_three]

/-- Over `ℚ` the witness has rank `3`. -/
theorem trap3_rank_rat : (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = 3 := by
  have := (rank_rat_full_iff_det_ne_zero trap3).2 (by rw [trap3_det]; norm_num)
  simpa using this

/-- Over `𝔽₂` the same witness has rank `2` — the value a correct instrument
must return and a `ℚ`-instrument does not. -/
theorem trap3_rank_zmod2 : (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = 2 := by
  set A := trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) with hA
  have hlt : A.rank ≠ 3 := by
    intro h
    have h' : A.rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3) := by simpa using h
    rw [hA, rank_zmod2_full_iff_odd_det, trap3_det] at h'
    exact absurd h' (by decide)
  have hle : A.rank ≤ 3 := by simpa using A.rank_le_card_width
  have hsub : (A.submatrix (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
      (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))).rank = 2 := by
    have : (A.submatrix (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
        (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))).det ≠ 0 := by
      rw [Matrix.det_fin_two]
      simp [hA, trap3]
    simpa using (rank_eq_card_iff_det_ne_zero _).2 this
  have hge := rank_submatrix_le_of_field A (fun i : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc i))
    (fun j : Fin 2 => (Fin.castSucc j))
  omega

/-- The witness is discriminating, as the criterion predicts (`det = 2`). -/
theorem trap3_discriminates :
    ¬ ((trap3.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3) ↔
      (trap3.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank = Fintype.card (Fin 3)) := by
  rw [full_rank_agree_iff, trap3_det]
  simp

/-! ## The error is one-sided -/

/-- Independence mod 2 lifts to independence over `ℤ`. -/
theorem linearIndependent_int_of_zmod2 {ι m : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (v : ι → m → ℤ)
    (h : LinearIndependent (ZMod 2) (fun i => fun k => ((v i k : ℤ) : ZMod 2))) :
    LinearIndependent ℤ v := by
  rw [Fintype.linearIndependent_iff] at h ⊢
  have key : ∀ e : ℕ, ∀ g : ι → ℤ, ∑ i, g i • v i = 0 → ∀ i, (2 : ℤ) ^ e ∣ g i := by
    intro e
    induction e with
    | zero => intro g _ i; simp
    | succ e ih =>
      intro g hg i
      have heven : ∀ j, (2 : ℤ) ∣ g j := by
        intro j
        have h2 := h (fun j => (g j : ZMod 2)) (by
          funext k
          have := congrFun hg k
          simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.zero_apply] at this ⊢
          have := congrArg (Int.cast : ℤ → ZMod 2) this
          push_cast at this
          exact this) j
        exact (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd (g j) 2).1 h2
      choose g' hg' using heven
      have hrel : ∑ j, g' j • v j = 0 := by
        have h2 : (2 : ℤ) • ∑ j, g' j • v j = 0 := by
          rw [← hg, Finset.smul_sum]
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_)
          rw [hg' j, SemigroupAction.mul_smul]
        funext k
        have := congrFun h2 k
        simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.zero_apply] at this ⊢
        omega
      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := ih g' hrel i
      exact ⟨c, by rw [hg' i, hc]; ring⟩
  intro g hg i
  have hd := key (g i).natAbs g hg i
  by_contra hne
  have hd' : 2 ^ (g i).natAbs ∣ (g i).natAbs := by
    have := Int.natAbs_dvd_natAbs.2 hd
    simpa [Int.natAbs_pow] using this
  have h1 := Nat.le_of_dvd (Int.natAbs_pos.2 hne) hd'
  have h2 : (g i).natAbs < 2 ^ (g i).natAbs := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  omega

/-- **One-sided error.**  For every integer matrix, the `𝔽₂`-rank is at most the
`ℚ`-rank: an instrument that silently returns the `ℚ`-rank can only
*overestimate* the `𝔽₂`-rank. -/
theorem rank_zmod2_le_rank_rat {m n : Type*} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℤ) :
    (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).rank ≤ (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).rank := by
  classical
  rw [rank_eq_finrank_span_cols, rank_eq_finrank_span_cols]
  obtain ⟨κ, a, ha, hspan, hli⟩ :=
    exists_linearIndependent' (ZMod 2) (A.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))).col
  have : Finite κ := Finite.of_injective a ha
  have : Fintype κ := Fintype.ofFinite κ
  rw [← hspan, finrank_span_eq_card hli]
  have hZ : LinearIndependent ℤ (fun k => A.col (a k)) :=
    linearIndependent_int_of_zmod2 _ hli
  set f : (m → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (m → ℚ) := (Int.castAddHom ℚ).toIntLinearMap.compLeft m with hf
  have hfinj : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥ := by
    rw [LinearMap.ker_eq_bot]
    intro x y hxy
    funext i
    have := congrFun hxy i
    simpa [hf] using this
  have hZQ : LinearIndependent ℤ (f ∘ fun k => A.col (a k)) := hZ.map' f hfinj
  have hQ : LinearIndependent ℚ (fun k => (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).col (a k)) := by
    rw [← LinearIndependent.iff_fractionRing ℤ ℚ]
    exact hZQ
  rw [← finrank_span_eq_card hQ]
  haveI : FiniteDimensional ℚ
      (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)).col)) :=
    FiniteDimensional.span_of_finite ℚ (Set.finite_range _)
  apply Submodule.finrank_mono
  apply Submodule.span_mono
  rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨a k, rfl⟩

end GF2RankTrap
